o1.biggest_strength: It builds the whole plan from the data: Spark Ads on the nurse and server videos from day 1, problem-first hooks in Maria's own words, and a day-30 bar of $38 tied to the 90-day break-even.
o1.biggest_mistake: The 90-day contribution is stated as about $38.50 when the brief's working gives about $38 (the fee estimate of $9.90 vs about $10 is slightly off), and the 'new customers up 70% of claimed orders' test is a bit convoluted for a Monday handoff.
o1.what_would_make_it_a_10: Give the exact 90-day contribution figure with its working ($48.40 minus about $10) and a one-line, clean day-30 stop/go rule.

o2.biggest_strength: It nails the money logic ($27.10 first-order, $38.46 over 90 days, $57 cut line, $114 per-ad test) and turns the data into specific moves: both licensed worker videos as Spark Ads from Day 1, problem-first openers, and a three-read day-30 verdict.
o2.biggest_mistake: It spends slightly less aggressively early than the opportunity merits ($800/day flat for the first two weeks vs. a tighter ramp), and the day-30 verdict leans heavily on a three-read structure that assumes the survey and blended baseline are clean.
o2.what_would_make_it_a_10: Add an explicit dollar lifetime-value check on the day-30 decision so the scale/stop call is bulletproof.

reason: Both are strong and use the data well, but Output 2's numbers are cleaner and its set-up, kill/scale rules and day-30 test are the most Monday-ready; Output 1 is close behind and would need only small tweaks.
